title: Chili Piper Chat Competitors vs Storylane RepX
summary: Chili Piper alternatives for AI chat and scheduling: real 2026 pricing, where each tool fits, and how to keep your routing. Storylane RepX + 5 more.
body_markdown:
*Last updated: October 2026. Pricing and product facts were re-checked against each vendor's own site this month.*


Most Chili Piper alternatives lists solve the wrong problem. I'm Madhav Bhandari, CMO at Storylane, and my argument is blunt: if you are shopping for a Chili Piper alternative because of its chat, nearly every ranking guide hands you a list of scheduling tools you never asked about.


The pain you actually have is usually chat-specific. You want a website conversation that qualifies a visitor and routes them to the right rep, fast, without ripping out the meeting logic you already built. So this piece treats the chat layer, Chili Piper's Chat AI and Concierge Live, as the thing under evaluation, and judges every alternative on how it handles a live visitor. If you really are replacing the scheduling and routing engine too, there is a dedicated section for that below.


> **Definition:** A Chili Piper Chat alternative is a tool that replaces or augments Chili Piper's live website chat and concierge routing, not its scheduling widget. It is evaluated on conversational qualification, response speed, and live-agent handoff, not on calendar availability rules.


## Chili Piper alternatives at a glance


Here is the shortlist, with each vendor's published pricing as of October 2026. The first four are chat-first; the last three are scheduling-first tools for buyers replacing Chili Piper's routing and calendar engine.


Tool Best for Standout capability Pricing model (published) Where it falls short


**Storylane RepX** Chat plus interactive demo in one flow AI agent that qualifies, answers from your content, shows the product, and books From $2,000/mo (up to 20,000 monthly visitors); 30-day free trial Not a scheduling or routing engine; pair with your router


**Qualified** Salesforce-first inbound teams Piper AI SDR across website chat, voice, video and email, with meeting booking Quote-based; prices not public Built around Salesforce; now Salesforce-owned


**Intercom Fin** Support-led chat with sales overlap Fin AI Agent, averaging 76% resolution per fin.ai From $29/seat/mo (Essential, annual) plus $0.99 per Fin outcome Support-tuned; costs scale with conversation volume


**OnceHub** Chatbot-led scheduling on a budget Chatbots with NLP plus AI-driven and rule-based routing on its Engage plan Schedule $10, Route $19, Engage $39 per user/mo (annual) Scheduling-first; lighter AI qualification than an AI SDR


**Default** Replacing form routing and scheduling Form routing, scheduling, enrichment and workflow automation Growth $1,250/mo ($15,000/yr); Scale $3,000/mo No website chat product


**RevenueHero** Transparent per-user routing and scheduling Books from forms and from your existing chat widget Inbound: $79/mo platform fee plus $25/user/mo (annual) No AI chat agent of its own


**Drift** Not recommended for new buyers Mature playbook chat Being sunset; existing clients referred to 1mind Sunset announced March 5, 2026


## What "Chili Piper Chat" actually is (and why most alternatives lists get this wrong)


Chili Piper is not one product. Its site lists Form Concierge, Chat AI, a Routing and Scheduling AI platform, Distro, Handoff, and ChiliCal, with Concierge Live and AI agents working across them. Those are different jobs, and a team frustrated with one is often perfectly happy with the others.


That distinction is exactly what the SERP misses. Almost every page ranking for "Chili Piper alternatives" reviews the scheduling and routing side only, then recommends meeting-booking tools. Those are fine at that job. If your problem is the chat window on your site, though, that list answers a question you did not ask.


Where chat tools sit inside a broader[modern sales tech stack](https://www.storylane.io/blog/tools-to-build-the-best-sales-tech-stack) matters, but the buying decision here is narrower: the conversation a visitor has before they ever see a calendar.


## What Chili Piper Chat (Chat AI + Concierge Live) actually does


Chili Piper describes Chat AI as "your always-on conversion assistant" that qualifies visitors, answers questions, and books meetings 24/7. Concierge Live is the piece that connects a qualified visitor to a live rep on the spot, the concierge-routing behavior Chili Piper is known for. Together they aim at one outcome: turn an anonymous website visit into a routed, qualified conversation without a form-fill dead end.


It is worth being fair: when it is configured well and a visitor is on a high-intent page, chatting, qualifying, and dropping into a booked meeting is smooth. Here is what the chat line is built to do:


- Greet and engage visitors on high-intent pages in real time.
- Ask qualification questions and answer product questions.
- Route qualified visitors to the right rep or team, using existing ownership rules.
- Offer instant meeting booking once a visitor clears qualification.
- Hand a live conversation to a human when the moment calls for it.


The catch is packaging. On[Chili Piper's pricing page](https://www.chilipiper.com/pricing) , the base Routing and Scheduling plan includes live chat with a team member, while the AI-powered, around-the-clock chat sits in the higher Experiences tier. I come back to the numbers in the pricing section.


## Why teams look for a Chili Piper Chat alternative specifically


People rarely go shopping because a product is bad. With Chili Piper Chat, the blockers cluster around three themes, and the right alternative depends on which one is yours.


**Pricing and packaging.** AI chat is in the Experiences tier, which starts at $42,000/year ($3,500/month) with 30 seats, versus $15,000/year ($1,250/month) with 15 seats for Routing and Scheduling, per Chili Piper's pricing page. For a team that loves the scheduling engine but only wants AI chat, that is a steep step up. Framing chat within a wider[enterprise sales software stack](https://www.storylane.io/blog/enterprise-sales-software) helps decide whether the premium is worth it.


**Performance on the page.** Chat lives in the browser, and a heavy widget can slow the very pages it is supposed to convert. Load time belongs near the top of your checklist.


**Purpose-built versus bolted-on.** Chili Piper's core is routing and scheduling, and chat sits on top of that engine. That is a strength if routing is your priority and a question to test if conversational depth is. The pattern I see most often is teams that want to keep their Chili Piper routing logic and add a smarter conversation in front of it, not rebuild routing from scratch.


## How to evaluate a Chili Piper Chat alternative


Here is the framework I would use, in order of how much it moves conversion. Score each tool one to five on every line.


- **Response time to first message.** A chat that lags for several seconds loses the intent it was meant to catch.
- **AI qualification depth versus keyword routing.** Can the tool reason about what a visitor says, or is it matching keywords to a decision tree? This is the heart of[qualifying inbound leads in real time](https://www.storylane.io/blog/the-ultimate-guide-to-sales-qualification) .
- **Live-agent handoff quality.** When the AI reaches its limit, does it pass the visitor, with full context, to a human?
- **Native fit with your existing scheduling and CRM stack.** Does it layer onto the routing and CRM you already run, or force a rip-and-replace?
- **Pricing transparency.** Is chat priced clearly, or gated behind a top tier you have to buy wholesale?


### Widget performance and setup complexity


Two practical checks sit underneath the framework. The first is page performance. Chili Piper's scheduling widget draws repeated load-time complaints in user reviews, but I have not seen independent testing of the Chat widget specifically, so treat any precise load-time claim as an assumption, not a measurement. Run your own test instead: load the chat on a staging copy of your highest-traffic page and compare page speed with and without it, and ask each vendor for production references at your traffic level.


The second is setup weight. Rules-based chat needs if-then flows authored and maintained for every branch, and each branch you did not anticipate is a visitor who hits a dead end. AI qualification reduces that work but does not remove it. Ask every vendor for a realistic time-to-value for a team your size, because every week of configuration is a week the tool is not catching visitors.


Controllability belongs inside criteria two and three: teams want to watch conversations and correct the AI quickly when it says something wrong. Weight the framework to your reality: a team drowning in unqualified inbound should over-index on qualification depth, while a high-touch sales floor cares most about handoff.


## The real Chili Piper Chat competitors, compared


A real Chili Piper Chat competitor does the same job Chili Piper Chat does: it engages and qualifies a live visitor before a form fill, hands off to a rep, and gets a meeting booked. By that test there are four chat-first tools worth comparing today: Storylane RepX, Qualified, Intercom Fin, and OnceHub. Drift was the fifth until its sunset, and Dashly is a smaller entrant to validate yourself. Calendars and routers are covered separately below, because they compete with Chili Piper's scheduling engine, not its chat.


Here is how each chat-first option handles a live visitor.


### Storylane RepX


Full disclosure: this is us.[RepX](https://www.storylane.io/repx) is Storylane's AI agent for your website (see how it compares among the[best AI SDR tools](https://www.storylane.io/blog/top-ai-sdr-tools) ). It is trained on your docs, website, decks, call scripts, and interactive demos, so it answers specific product questions, handles objections, qualifies against your ICP, and books meetings, across text and voice, with a video avatar on Premium. When a buyer wants to see the product, it pulls up the relevant interactive demo inside the conversation, rather than stopping at a name and an email. That is the move that helps you[convert more demo requests](https://www.storylane.io/blog/demo-requests) .


Playbooks let you run a different qualification flow per page, and qualified leads and conversation summaries flow to HubSpot, Salesforce, and Slack. Pricing is published: Growth from $2,000/month for up to 20,000 monthly visitors, Premium from $3,000/month for up to 60,000 visitors, with a 30-day free trial, per[storylane.io/plans](https://www.storylane.io/plans) . That is well under Chili Piper's $42,000/year Experiences tier on an annualized basis.


Where it does not fit: RepX is not a routing or calendar engine, so if you want to keep Chili Piper's routing, plan the handoff between the two in your evaluation. And if you want a pure support-deflection bot, or you have no interactive demo motion at all, a lighter chat tool may serve you better. For a related head-to-head, see[Spara vs Chili Piper](https://www.storylane.io/blog/spara-vs-chili-piper) .


### Qualified


Qualified is the strongest fit for Salesforce-first teams. Its AI SDR, Piper, meets buyers on the website over video, voice, or live chat, follows up by email, and books meetings, per[qualified.com](https://www.qualified.com/piper) . Salesforce completed its acquisition of Qualified on April 1, 2026, and every Qualified plan on its pricing page is built around the Salesforce integration. Prices are not published. We go deeper in our[Chili Piper vs Qualified comparison](https://www.storylane.io/blog/chili-piper-vs-qualified) and our[Qualified alternatives](https://www.storylane.io/blog/qualified-alternatives) guide.


The flip side is gravity: if your CRM and routing already live in Salesforce, Qualified feels native. If they do not, you inherit a philosophy that assumes Salesforce is the center of your universe.


### Intercom Fin


Intercom Fin comes at chat from the support world, and it is very good at that job. Fin's site says it averages a 76% resolution rate across 12,000+ customers, and it costs $0.99 per outcome on top of Intercom seats starting at $29/seat/month, per intercom.com/pricing. See how the two stack up in our[Chili Piper vs Intercom comparison](https://www.storylane.io/blog/chili-piper-vs-intercom) .


The caveat is intent. Fin is tuned to resolve and deflect, not to qualify and route a high-intent buyer into a sales motion, and on a high-traffic marketing site a per-outcome bill scales with volume rather than with pipeline.


### OnceHub


OnceHub is the honest budget option, and it earns a place because its chatbot-led scheduling sits closer to Chili Piper's territory than a plain calendar tool. Its Engage plan ($39/user/month on annual billing) includes unlimited chatbots with natural language processing and AI-driven and rule-based routing; Route ($19/user/month) adds conversational forms, per oncehub.com/pricing.


Match it to the job: it is a scheduling-first platform with chatbots, not an AI SDR trained on your product. For a smaller team testing whether chat-led booking moves the needle before an enterprise contract, it is a sensible, low-risk start.


### Dashly


Dashly is the least-known name here. Its site describes AI agents that engage, qualify, and book inbound leads around the clock across web chat, WhatsApp, Telegram, and email, which puts it on the same axis as Chili Piper Chat rather than against a scheduler. The public record on its qualification accuracy and fit for larger B2B teams is thin, so ask for reference customers at your size and a live look at the bot-to-rep handoff before you weigh it against the better-documented tools above.


### Drift (sunset: not recommended for new buyers)


Drift built the conversational-marketing category, and its playbook chat was mature. But on March 5, 2026, Clari + Salesloft announced "the gradual sunset" of Drift and an exclusive agreement to refer existing Drift clients to 1mind, per the[Salesloft newsroom](https://www.salesloft.com/company/newsroom/1-mind-partnership) . I would not steer a team onto a platform being sunset. If you are on Drift today, see our[Drift alternatives](https://www.storylane.io/blog/drift-alternatives) guide and[Chili Piper vs Drift](https://www.storylane.io/blog/chili-piper-vs-drift) .


## Chili Piper alternatives for scheduling-plus-chat buyers


If you searched "Chili Piper alternatives" because you want to replace the routing and scheduling engine as well, the market looks different. These tools replace Form Concierge, routing, and calendars. None of them is an AI chat agent, so the realistic stack is a scheduling tool plus a chat layer.


That is also why Calendly, Default, and RevenueHero, which dominate many "Chili Piper alternatives" lists, are not Chili Piper Chat competitors. The dividing line is one sentence:


- **Scheduling tools act after intent is captured:** they route, round-robin, and book someone who already filled a form.
- **Chat tools act before intent is captured:** they open a conversation with a visitor who has not raised their hand yet.


If you have already captured intent and just need clean routing and booking, a scheduler is the cheaper, simpler answer. If the visitors you are losing are the ones who never fill a form, no scheduler will reach them.


- **Default:** form routing, lead distribution, scheduling, enrichment, and workflow automation, with CRM sync to Salesforce and HubSpot. Growth is $1,250/month ($15,000/year) and Scale is $3,000/month, with routing-plus-scheduling seats at $540/year per user, per default.com/pricing. Its site does not describe a website chat product.
- **RevenueHero:** routing and scheduling with transparent pricing (inbound: $79/month platform fee plus $25/user/month on annual billing, per revenuehero.io/pricing). It can book from forms and from "the chat widget in the corner," and syncs to HubSpot, Salesforce, or Attio, but it does not offer its own AI chat agent.
- **OnceHub:** covered above; the one scheduling-first option here with built-in chatbots.


The pattern that works: pick the scheduler for routing rules and price, then put an AI chat agent in front of it, such as RepX, Qualified, or Fin, depending on whether you want demo-led qualification, Salesforce-native AI, or support deflection. Ask both vendors to show the handoff live. Our guides to[Chili Piper vs live chat tools](https://www.storylane.io/blog/chili-piper-vs-live-chat) and[lead routing](https://www.storylane.io/blog/lead-routing) go deeper.


## Chili Piper Chat vs. the alternatives, feature by feature


This comparison uses the levers that decide a chat evaluation: how a tool qualifies, how it hands off, how it books, whether it can demo, and how it prices.

Two things jump out. First, real-time response and some form of handoff are table stakes now. Second, the real differentiators are qualification depth and what happens after qualification, which is where the interactive-demo row separates RepX. Shade every cell green, amber, or red for your situation; the tool with the fewest reds against your non-negotiables wins.


## What chat actually costs across these tools


Chili Piper's AI chat is not part of the base plan. To get it you step up from Routing and Scheduling at $15,000/year to Experiences at $42,000/year, a $27,000 annual difference, per Chili Piper's pricing page. Experiences also adds more seats (30 vs 15), more AI credits, account identification, and ABM targeting, so it is not purely a chat premium. We break down every line in our[Chili Piper Chat pricing guide](https://www.storylane.io/blog/chili-piper-chat-pricing) .


Tool How chat is priced What that means for a chat buyer


Chili Piper Chat AI chat in Experiences ($42,000/yr); base plan ($15,000/yr) includes live chat with a team member You buy the top tier to get AI chat


Storylane RepX From $2,000/mo by monthly visitors; 30-day free trial Priced as an AI agent plus demos, not chat alone


Qualified Quote-based (Premier, Enterprise, Ultimate) Best value if Salesforce is your core


Intercom Fin From $29/seat/mo plus $0.99 per outcome Costs scale with conversation volume


OnceHub Chatbots on Engage, $39/user/mo (annual) Low cost, scheduling-first


The math that matters is not the license fee; it is the cost per qualified, routed conversation. A cheaper tool that hands sales unqualified names can cost more in wasted rep time than a pricier tool that only forwards buyers who are ready. When you request quotes, ask each vendor to isolate the chat and qualification line item.


## Which Chili Piper alternative fits which team


If you are weighing specific rivals, our head-to-head guides cover[Chili Piper vs 1mind](https://www.storylane.io/blog/chili-piper-vs-1mind) and[Chili Piper vs Warmly](https://www.storylane.io/blog/chili-piper-vs-warmly) . Here is how I would match tool to motion:


- **AI-led qualification before any form:** Qualified if you are Salesforce-first, or RepX if you want qualification plus a product experience in the same conversation.
- **Strong live-agent handoff for high-touch deals:** Chili Piper Concierge Live and Qualified both cover this; let CRM fit and price break the tie.
- **Chat and interactive demos in one flow:** RepX.
- **Support-style deflection with some sales overlap:** Intercom Fin.
- **Structured chatbot booking on a budget:** OnceHub.
- **Replacing the scheduling and routing engine:** Default or RevenueHero, paired with an AI chat layer.


Whatever you choose, make integration with your existing routing a hard requirement in the demo. Ask the vendor to show your ownership rules firing through their chat, live, before you sign. Any of these paths should help you[book more discovery calls](https://www.storylane.io/blog/discovery-call-agenda) , which is the point of putting chat on the site at all.


## Conclusion: how to choose


Strip away the noise and the decision is smaller than it looks. Run the five-part framework, score your top two tools on the two criteria you refuse to compromise on, and confirm the winner layers onto the routing you already trust. That is how you pick among Chili Piper alternatives without getting dragged into a scheduling comparison you did not want.


My honest read: if you are Salesforce-first and want deep qualification, look hard at Qualified. If chat is really a support job, Fin earns its place. If you want budget chatbot booking, OnceHub is fair. And if the outcome you care about is moving a qualified visitor into an actual product experience in the same conversation, that is where RepX is built to win. The tool that most directly[shortens your sales cycle](https://www.storylane.io/blog/how-to-shorten-your-sales-cycle) for your motion is the right one.


## FAQ


### What is the best alternative to Chili Piper?


For the chat layer: Storylane RepX if you want an AI agent that also shows your product, Qualified if you are Salesforce-first, Intercom Fin for support-led chat, or OnceHub for budget chatbot scheduling. For the scheduling and routing engine: Default or RevenueHero, paired with an AI chat tool.


### Who are Chili Piper's main competitors?


It depends on which Chili Piper product you mean. For Chat, the competitors are chat-first tools that engage and qualify live visitors: Storylane RepX, Qualified, Intercom Fin, and OnceHub, with Drift being sunset and Dashly a smaller entrant. For routing and scheduling, the competitors are tools like Default, RevenueHero, and Calendly.


### Does Chili Piper's chat feature cost extra?


The AI-powered chat sits in the Experiences tier, which starts at $42,000/year, while the Routing and Scheduling base plan starts at $15,000/year and includes live chat with a team member, per Chili Piper's pricing page (October 2026).


### Is Chili Piper Chat the same product as its scheduling widget?


No. Chili Piper lists separate lines: Form Concierge, Chat AI, the Routing and Scheduling platform, Distro, Handoff, and ChiliCal, with Concierge Live connecting visitors to live reps. A chat evaluation is not a scheduling evaluation.


### Are Calendly and RevenueHero real Chili Piper Chat competitors?


Not for Chat. They are scheduling and routing tools that book meetings after a form fill and do not hold a live conversation with an anonymous visitor. They compete with Chili Piper's scheduling engine, and they pair well with a separate AI chat layer.


### Can I add a new chat tool without losing Chili Piper's existing routing logic?


Usually, yes, and it is the concern buyers raise most often. Decide which tool owns the conversation and which owns routing and booking, then ask each vendor to demonstrate the handoff live on your rules before you sign.


### Will a new chat tool conflict with a chatbot we already run?


It should not, if you scope it deliberately. Decide which tool owns which pages or intents so two conversational tools are not competing for the same visitor.
